fixes.explanation: Babylon is a name you may know, but it doesn't show up anywhere in these verses. God says, “Look at Assyria, a cedar in Lebanon…” Assyria is the nation pictured as the cedar. Good guess, though, friend.

False is right, friend. God says, “The cedars in the garden of God could not rival it…” The cypresses couldn't compare with its branches, and the plane trees couldn't match its boughs. This tree had no competition.

The text says the opposite. After the cedar is cut down, “…all the peoples of the earth left its shade and abandoned it.” They left, so they aren't staying. That's a quiet, sad moment for a tree that had the great nations living in its shade.
On the fallen trunk, baker. The text says, “All the birds of the air nested on its fallen trunk…” The tree is lying down now. That's a big change from the high branches.
The clouds are where the cedar's top used to be, back in verse 3. The text doesn't put the birds there, though. It says they “…nested on its fallen trunk…” That's the tree lying down, friend.
Yes, baker. The text says, “…all the trees of the field fainted because of it.” God also says He made Lebanon mourn for it. The trees of the field are reacting to the fall.
The text doesn't say that. It says, “…all the trees of the field fainted because of it.” God also says He made Lebanon mourn for it. The verse tells us they react to the fall by fainting.
The verse goes the other way. God says He made Lebanon mourn for the cedar, and “…all the trees of the field fainted because of it.” That's mourning, not celebrating.
Quake, friend. God says, “I made the nations quake at the sound of its downfall…” The sound of the downfall is what sets them quaking. God is the One who made it happen.
Cheering isn't in the verse, baker. God says, “I made the nations quake at the sound of its downfall…” That's shaking, not celebrating. The sound of the downfall is what moves the nations.
No singing here, friend. The text says, “I made the nations quake at the sound of its downfall…” The sound of the downfall is what shakes them. They quake instead.
Allies, baker! The text says, “As its allies they had lived in its shade among the nations.” So these trees were its allies, living under the same big branches. They went down with it.
The verse doesn't call them strangers. It says, “As its allies they had lived in its shade among the nations.” They're called its allies, and they lived in its shade.

True. God says to Pharaoh, “You also will be brought down to the depths of the earth to be with the trees of Eden.” The message started with Pharaoh's greatness and ends with Pharaoh himself. The text says it plainly.
It's actually true. God says, “You also will be brought down to the depths of the earth to be with the trees of Eden.” The line is spoken right to Pharaoh. The words just stand.
